page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by 192 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Neoverse-V2 ARM64 processor architecture running at 2.7 GHz. The system features 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. While single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category, the massive 192-core parallel architecture achieves top-tier multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, ranking in the top tier for both small cached blocks and large uncached read/write operations. However, LLM text generation speeds represent a notable tradeoff, registering as weak for both small 135M and large 70B models, though prompt processing speeds remain average to strong.

Given its bare-metal resource density and high memory bandwidth, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. It is suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing. Conversely, it is less suitable for workloads dependent on high single-thread performance or real-time LLM text generation.
